title: Linux Secure by Default. Are we there yet?
summary:
Linux has gained an impressive collection of security features over the last two decades. The Kernel Self Protection Project (KSPP), compiler-assisted hardening, seccomp, mandatory access control systems, and more recent memory-safety initiatives have made life harder for attackers.

Yet in the embedded world, products are often built on kernels several years old, security features are selectively enabled, and applications frequently run with privileges that would be considered excessive on a desktop or cloud system.

During my work with embedded companies, I regularly encounter a striking contrast: upstream Linux is becoming increasingly secure by default, while many deployed devices continue to rely on only a small subset of the protections available to them.

This talk explores that gap.

Using examples from embedded Linux systems, Yocto Project-based products, and upstream kernel development, we will examine how Linux performs against key security principles such as least privilege, attack-surface reduction, isolation, exploit mitigation, and memory safety. We will look at the progress achieved through KSPP and related initiatives, discuss why some security mechanisms are widely deployed while others remain rare in embedded products, and evaluate how close Linux is to being secure by default in practice.

The goal is not to review every security feature in the kernel, but to answer a practical question relevant to both kernel developers and product builders: Have we reached the point where a modern embedded Linux device is secure by default, or are the hardest problems now outside the kernel itself?

Marta Rybczynska
ja_summary:
・近年のLinuxはカーネルの保護機能が大幅に強化され、標準で高度なセキュリティを備えつつある。
・一方で組み込み機器では古いカーネルや一部機能の無効化が常態化しており、最新の防御策が十分に活用されていない。
・本講演では、組み込みLinuxの現状と課題を分析し、現実的な「デフォルトでの安全性」がどの程度実現されているかを考察する。

title: Using GitHub Copilot Safely: What Developers Need to Know About AI, Dependencies and Security
summary:
GitHub Copilot can make developers dramatically faster, but giving AI more access to our code, terminal, dependencies and development tools also introduces new security considerations.

In this practical session, we'll look at some of the security risks developers should be aware of when using GitHub Copilot and AI-assisted development workflows.

Using recent real-world npm supply-chain attacks as a case study, we'll explore how malicious code can enter a seemingly trusted development environment and why developers need to think beyond just the code they write.

We'll cover practical advice around:

* Reviewing AI-generated code and commands
* Understanding what Copilot and agents have access to
* MCP tools and permissions
* npm packages and dependency security
* Secrets, tokens and credentials
* Repository and developer-tool configuration
* CI/CD security
* Human review and useful guardrails

The goal is not to discourage developers from using Copilot. It's to help us use it confidently while understanding the new security responsibilities that come with AI-assisted development.
ja_summary:
GitHub Copilot等のAI開発ツールは生産性を高める一方、コードや外部ツールへのアクセス権限に関連した新たなセキュリティリスクを伴う。
AIが生成したコードや依存パッケージの検証、認証情報や権限の適切な管理など、安全な運用のためのガードレール構築が不可欠である。
AI活用の利便性を享受しつつ、開発環境全体に対する責任範囲を正しく理解し、人間によるレビュー体制を整えることが重要。

title: Scalable Angular Architectures with Route-Based Architecture
summary: Architecture decisions in Angular often start with the routes. In this talk, Fabian Gosebrink shows how clean modules, libraries, and state areas can be derived from routing structures. With Nx, he supports modularization and keeps dependencies under control. The result: an architecture that grows with its requirements and gives teams clear orientation. Attendees learn how to structure complex applications along their routes and keep them maintainable over the long term.
ja_summary:
・Angularのルーティング構造を基盤に、モジュールやライブラリを適切に配置する設計手法を解説。
・Nxを活用して依存関係を制御し、要件の変化に強く拡張性の高いアプリケーションを構築する。
・複雑なシステムにおいても開発チームが迷わず、長期的な保守性を維持できるアーキテクチャを実現する。

title: Why State Is the Most Important Part of Your Angular Application
summary: State is the foundation of every modern Angular application. A well-structured state management strategy determines not only how data flows through an application but also how scalable, maintainable, and performant it becomes. Without proper state management, applications quickly become hard to debug, difficult to scale, and prone to inconsistencies. This talk explores why state is the most crucial part of an Angular application, how to choose the right state management approach, and what common pitfalls to avoid. Whether using NgRx, the Signal Store, Signals, or a simple service-based approach, understanding and structuring state effectively is the key to long-term success.
ja_summary:
・Angularアプリにおいて、状態管理は拡張性・保守性・パフォーマンスを左右する最も重要な要素である。
・管理が不適切だとバグや不整合の原因となるため、適切な戦略の選択が不可欠である。
・NgRxやSignalsなど手法に関わらず、効果的な状態の設計こそがアプリの長期的な成功を決定づける。
